one_line_contribution: A crossover identification device for agentic-memory evaluation: holding the optimized instruction and the test instances fixed, compare the gain of the bank distilled from the very episodes that instruction was optimized on (own) against the gain of a bank from episodes the optimizer never saw (other), so that the shrinkage of memory's benefit under prompt optimization can be attributed to information the instruction absorbed rather than to headroom it consumed — with a fix/break signature to separate absorption from interference, and a compiled-bank arm token-matched against live per-instance retrieval.
closest_prior_work: Two, in different ways. (a) EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202) is the empirical threat: it already puts ReasoningBank (+3.6), Memento (-2.4) and GEPA (+1.2) on the same 528/267 trajectories on Qwen3.5-27B — one of this proposal's own candidate agents — so a reviewer can read 'an optimizer given the same episodes nearly matches a memory retriever' directly off a published table, which is most of the rhetorical force of the title. The proposal is right that it lacks combined optimizer+memory cells, token matching, a compiled arm and paired statistics, so the *attribution* is not pre-empted; but it caps how surprising the headline can be. (b) MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695) is the conceptual threat: instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint optimization on one training set is exactly the two-container ablation, with the published finding that the split is task-dependent. The proposal's genuine deltas over MIPROv2 are the query-conditioned read, distillation, and the held-out-episode crossover — real, but incremental. Neither runs the own-vs-other contrast, so novelty survives; it survives as a refinement of attribution on a question the field has already half-answered, not as a new question.
strongest_objection: The design is very likely to terminate in one of its own fallback branches, and every branch is a weaker paper than the title. Do the arithmetic on gate G7: the crossover (cells 5-10) only carries a confirmatory claim if the *unseen* bank M_b still adds >=4pt (lower 80% CI >=2pt) on top of an optimized instruction I1a, and then Prediction 1 additionally needs own to trail other by >=2pt. So the study needs roughly a 4-6pt memory effect surviving prompt optimization on a 27-32B agent in BM25 multi-hop QA. The proposal's own cited priors say that is implausible: this program's pilot measured +0.6pt, 90% CI [-1.2, +2.5], TOST-equivalent to zero for an ExpeL bank on Qwen3.5-27B, and EvoAgentBench's best method on that same backbone is +3.6pt at a *hand-written* prompt — i.e. below the G1 bar of 4pt before any optimizer is applied, and necessarily smaller after. The pre-registered consequence of a G7 failure is that the primary becomes 'the headroom share and the ladder' with the crossover run at 2 descriptive seeds, which means the paper's advertised contribution never gets tested at power. The second half of the objection is that the branch where G7 *passes* is not much better: the proposal concedes in Limitation 12 that BM25 multi-hop QA 'is not where procedural memory is expected to be most valuable', and the procedure for HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki is roughly one paragraph ('decompose, search the bridge entity, search the second hop') — precisely the content an instruction slot holds losslessly. A positive Delta_info there is close to tautological and environment-bound, and E2 cannot rescue it because ALFWorld's own treatment-free floor of 3.8-4.6pt at n=274 exceeds the 2pt claim threshold, so the one environment with genuinely compilable recurring procedure is definitionally incapable of supporting the claim. Heads the result is unsurprising and local, tails it is a null already reported by the program's own pilot.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Screen on the effect that the design actually needs. Make G7 — memory's gain at the *optimized* instruction — the selection criterion across agent x bank x *environment*, not a downstream gate applied after A1 was chosen by its I0 effect (G1). If no in-scope cell has a surviving memory effect large enough to admit a 2pt Delta_info, that finding is the paper and should be the pre-registered primary plan, not the fallback. 2) Move the confirmatory test to an environment with recurring multi-step subroutines (ALFWorld promoted to primary, or a tool/web agent benchmark), and power it below the claim threshold — more episodes, more decoding seeds, or a per-subgoal paired metric instead of binary task success — so E2's 3.8-4.6pt floor stops disqualifying the only setting where the phenomenon should live. Demote multi-hop QA to the replication it currently calls E2. 3) Promote cell 18c (I1a x M_a^re) to Tier 0, n=1000, 4 seeds. Prediction 5 is an equivalence claim ('within 2pt') and the wording-vs-provenance alternative (outcome ii'') is the one that most directly guts 'information-specific'; at n=500 with 1 decoding seed at I0 the TOST cannot resolve 2pt, so the arm defending the headline interpretation is underpowered relative to the arm producing it. 4) Pre-register sign consistency across both crossover directions as a condition on the claim rather than merely fitting and reporting the direction x half interaction — 'no consistency across directions is required' lets a large one-directional effect plus a bank-quality asymmetry produce a significant mean Delta_info with the mechanism unidentified. 5) Pay for all of this by cutting Tier 1 hard and by collapsing the Short Hypothesis, which currently bundles five distinct claims (Delta_info, full-data non-addition, compile-once equivalence, no I2 synergy, instance-specific residual) where the track brief asks for one sharp claim.
missing_baseline: A token-matched irrelevant-content control in the memory slot — a shuffled or randomly-drawn-item bank retrieved at k=7 and injected at the same token count, run at *both* I0 and I1a. It appears only as an unnumbered 'shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check' in the last line of Baselines and Ablations, with no cell number, no n, no seed count and no compute allocation, while 25 other cells get all four. Without it, a small residual own-bank gain at I1a cannot be separated from the format effect of having anything at all in the memory slot, and the compiled-arm TOST (cell 4 vs cell 2) has no null-content anchor. Second omission: an oracle-retrieval upper bound (the best item in B_a per test instance, chosen post hoc), without which a null Delta_info or a null residual is confounded with MiniLM top-7 retrieval quality — G3 certifies only 60% relevance on a 100-item audit, far too weak to license 'memory has no non-substitutable value'. Third, smaller: there is no *informed* hand-written instruction. I_H is explicitly information-free and C_a is an LLM compiler, so the practitioner's actual alternative — a human reads the 400 episodes or the bank and writes the instruction — is never run.
preprint_collision: This is the strongest section of the submission and should be credited as such: it is dated, it lists its channels (15 HF Papers queries, 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs, targeted web search), it names the paper that broke a prior novelty claim (EvoAgentBench, arXiv 2607.05202), and it *withdraws* the v2 sentence 'no published work uses one as the control for the other' rather than defending it. It also correctly flags that the compile direction (Prediction 7) is already pre-empted in sign by arXiv 2608.14036, 2606.30775 and 2605.23899, and restates it as a quantified equivalence. I am not aware of a preprint that runs the own-vs-other held-out-episode crossover, so I do not think the core is scooped. But the check's ground truth is fragile in ways that matter for the numbers it is load-bearing for. arXiv is unreachable from the node and Semantic Scholar was rate-limited, so abs pages were confirmed 'through web search results only'; the EvoAgentBench figures that set the G1 threshold and justify the whole screening design (+3.6/+1.2/-2.4 on Qwen3.5-27B) come from a PDF 'supplied by the PI' — an interested party, not an independent channel — after a web snippet had already misreported one of those numbers as +7; and the appendix of arXiv 2608.14036 is admitted to be unopened, which is exactly where the residual risk the proposal itself names ('a GEPA + memory ablation may exist in an appendix of a systems paper') would sit. Compounding this, the section documents a prior incident in which five citations were wrongly retracted as unverifiable and then reinstated, which establishes that this pipeline errs in both directions. I could verify the pre-2026 anchors (ExpeL 2308.10144, GEPA 2507.19457, ReasoningBank 2509.25140, Memp 2508.06433, A-MEM 2502.12110, MIPROv2 2406.11695); I cannot vouch for several 2026 IDs that fall within my own knowledge, including 'Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip' (2604.14585), MemAPO (2603.21520) and TERMS-Bench (2605.13909). Verdict on the check: thorough in procedure, not yet closed in fact — the re-run before design freeze that the proposal promises should include opening 2608.14036's appendix and confirming EvoAgentBench through a channel other than the PI.
